walkthroughs.body_html:
When a wave hits a barrier it can reflect — bounce back.

The angle of incidence (measured from the normal, not the surface) equals the angle of reflection. Always from the normal!

You see this with mirrors, echoes from a wall, and straight wavefronts bouncing off a barrier in a ripple tank.

When a wave crosses into a new medium it can change speed. If it hits the boundary at an angle, this change of speed makes it bend — that's refraction.

Water waves slow down when they cross from deep to shallow water in a ripple tank. As they slow, their wavelength gets shorter but their frequency stays the same.

A wavefront is a line joining bits of the wave that are doing the same thing at the same time — like the crest of a single ripple.

Straight wavefronts in deep water turn at a boundary and become straight wavefronts in shallow water travelling in a new direction.

In an exam, draw the wavefronts closer together where the wave is slower. 📏

mcqs.q: When a water wave moves from deep into shallow water, what happens?
options: Speed and wavelength both increase
Speed decreases and wavelength decreases, frequency stays the same
Frequency decreases, speed stays the same
Nothing changes

mcqs.q: The angle of incidence is measured between the incoming ray and what?
options: The surface
The reflected ray
The normal
The barrier edge

mcqs.q: When a wave travels through water, what happens to the water itself?
options: The water turns into wave material and changes state.
The water oscillates about a fixed point; the wave transfers energy, not matter.
The water moves along with the wave from one place to another.
The book emits a special invisible signal that your brain detects directly.

mcqs.q: How do you see a non-luminous object like a book?
options: The book emits a special invisible signal that your brain detects directly.
Your eyes send out beams of vision that hit the book and let you see it.
Light from a source reflects off the book and enters your eyes.
The speed of the wave determines pitch — faster waves sound higher.

mcqs.q: What property of a sound wave determines its pitch?
options: Amplitude determines pitch — a bigger wave is a higher-pitched note.
The speed of the wave determines pitch — faster waves sound higher.
The frequency — higher frequency means higher pitch.
The book emits a special invisible signal that your brain detects directly.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Wavefront”?
options: A shallow tray used to study water waves in the lab
A wave bouncing off a surface back into the same medium
A wave changing direction as it enters a new medium
A line joining points on a wave that are in step (in phase)

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Boundary”?
options: A wave changing direction as it enters a new medium
A shallow tray used to study water waves in the lab
A line joining points on a wave that are in step (in phase)
The edge where one medium meets another

The edge where one medium meets another
A shallow tray used to study water waves in the lab
A wave bouncing off a surface back into the same medium
